subject: Stan functions in R package, take 2

messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Stan functions in R package, take 2
parts:
I am writing a package that contains a stan model, and some functions 
that I wrote in Stan. I'd like the compiled functions to be included in the 
package. I know I could call

expose_stan_functions(mypackage:::stanmodels$mymodel)

but that's a bit ugly, and takes some time. 

What I have tried: 

- ran expose_stan_functions() and fished the cpp file out of tempdir()
- put the .cpp file in src/ 
- Tried building. That didn't work. I get the error: 

duplicate symbol __ZN4stan4lang15rethrow_locatedERKSt9exceptioni in:
    Modules.o
    make_shares.o
ld: 1 duplicate symbol for architecture x86_64

(make_shares.cpp is the renamed file I fished out of tempdir())

- Tried using Rcpp::Rcpp.package.skeleton() to create a new package with the .cpp file, then moved the src/Rcppexports.cpp into mypackage/src/ and R/RcppExports.R into mypackage/R/RcppExports.R
- Added the following to the top of Rcppexports.cpp

using stan::math::vector_d;
using stan::math::row_vector_d;
using stan::math::matrix_d;

But then I get a bunch of errors that look like this: 

RcppExports.cpp:20:59: error: no type named 'type' in the global namespace
    Rcpp::traits::input_parameter< const row_vector_d& >::type xi(xiSEXP);
                                                        ~~^
RcppExports.cpp:21:42: error: unknown type name 'matrix_d'
    Rcpp::traits::input_parameter< const matrix_d& >::type z(zSEXP);
                                         ^
RcppExports.cpp:21:55: error: no type named 'type' in the global namespace
    Rcpp::traits::input_parameter< const matrix_d& >::type z(zSEXP);

Any thoughts on what to try next? 

Jim

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Stan functions in R package, take 2
parts:
On Wednesday, April 5, 2017 at 5:21:26 PM UTC-4, James Savage wrote:
I realised I made a mistake in the Rcpp approach. The new error I get is: 

duplicate symbol __ZN4stan4lang15rethrow_locatedERKSt9exceptioni in:
    Modules.o
    RcppExports.o
duplicate symbol __ZN4stan4lang15rethrow_locatedERKSt9exceptioni in:
    Modules.o
    make_shares.o

We had trouble with the rethrow_located function before, but it shouldn't have anything to do with the functions you wrote. The expose_stan_functions() function includes a bunch of stuff that probably does not need to be included. You could try pruning some of the include statements from the .cpp file. But I don't of any R package that has accomplished this. It is probably doable, but perhaps is easier to write C++ functions that link to the Stan Math Library headers than to write Stan functions that get translated to those C++ functions.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Stan functions in R package, take 2
parts:
Or split the difference and use Stan to generate the functions,
then convert their types to primitives, then wrap in Rcpp.

This should get easier when we fix the generation for functions
in the modeling language to make them compilable standalone. As
is, RStan is hacking the generated C++ code with string matching.

- Bob
